name: Montview Heights (Montview Heights Apartments)
headline: Related Affordable plans to buy and renovate Montview Heights, an existing 50-unit, all-three-bedroom HUD Section 8 family property at 14389 East Montview Blvd in north Aurora (Adams County). It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA backed by Aurora Housing Authority bonds.
why_it_matters: This is a preservation deal. Every unit carries a project-based Section 8 contract that runs to 2040, and residents' average household income is about $21,000. The tax credit adds a 60% AMI restriction on all 50 large family units and pays for a rehab funded with Aurora Housing Authority bonds.

status.label: Credits awarded; bond hearing held March 2026; acquisition and closing not confirmed
status.detail: The Aurora Housing Authority held a public hearing on the bonds on 2026-03-20. No record of the bond closing, the property sale to Related's partnership, or the start of the rehab was found. HUD's data still lists Avail Property Management as the agent.

next_step: Watch for the Aurora mayor's approval of the bonds, a recorded deed to Montview Heights Preservation, L.P. in Adams County, and a HUD transfer (2530) or Section 8 contract assignment.

key_numbers.meaning: All 50 units are also covered by a HUD project-based Section 8 contract, so tenants pay rent based on income.
About $14.6M over 10 years, or roughly $292,000 of credit per unit. No state credit.
The amount CHFA prints, or about $346,000 per unit. The bond hearing notice allowed up to $25M for acquisition, rehabilitation and construction.

background.text: Montview Heights is a 50-unit family property built under HUD's Section 8 new construction program for state housing finance agency projects. HUD records its occupancy date as 1978-10-26 and lists it as previously insured, with no active HUD-insured financing.
The current Section 8 contract covers all 50 units and runs to 2040-03-31. The tax credit deal would add a 60% AMI LIHTC restriction on top of it.
The Aurora Housing Authority's hearing notice says bond proceeds will finance or reimburse the acquisition, rehabilitation, renovation, construction and equipping of the roughly 50-unit project.
The bonds are special, limited revenue obligations of the Authority; neither the City of Aurora nor the state is liable for them.
HUD's resident data shows mostly very low-income families with children: about 124 children among about 191 residents, and about 61% of households headed by women with children.
